title: Low-Volume Direct Analysis Urine Preparation for Non-Targeted GC-MS Metabolomics
author: Allen, Luies
materials: This section provides detailed instructions for preparing essential solutions, focusing on proper handling and storage to maintain accuracy and reliability.11.Prepare an internal standard solution:a.Prepare a 500 ppm stock solution:i.Weigh 25 mg of 3-phenylbutyric acid using a glass weighing boat, and transfer it to a 50 mL volumetric flask through its glass funnel.ii.Rinse the glass weighing boat twice with ∼2 mL milli-Q water.iii.Add milli-Q water to just below the 50 mL mark and swirl to dissolve.iv.Top up to the 50 mL mark with milli-Q water using a plastic dropper, cap, and shake gently.Note: If the solution does not dissolve, sonicate using an ultrasonic water bath sonicator for 20 min or until fully dissolved. Keep the volumetric flask capped during sonication to avoid contamination. If the solution still does not dissolve, refer to troubleshooting (problem 1) for guidance.b.Prepare a 50 ppm working solution:i.Pipette 5 mL of the 500 ppm solution into a 50 mL volumetric flask using a glass graduated pipette.ii.Fill to 50 mL with milli-Q water, using a plastic dropper for precise filling.iii.Transfer the solution to a clean, labeled 50 mL Schott bottle.c.Mark the bottles properly (contents, concentration, date, initials).Note: The 500 ppm stock solution and 50 ppm working solution can be stored at −80°C for up to 6 months or at −20°C for up to 1 month. If the solutions are older than this, prepare fresh to ensure optimal accuracy.12.Prepare the methoxyamine hydrochloride (MOX-HCl; 20 mg/mL):a.Weigh 20 mg of MOX-HCl using a glass weighing boat.b.Dissolve in 1 mL of pyridine using a Hamilton syringe (in a fume hood). If it does not dissolve, refer to troubleshooting (problem 2) for guidance.Note: Although this protocol describes the use of a Hamilton syringe, any similar high-precision syringe for handling small volumes will be appropriate.c.Transfer to a clean, marked GC vial (if the final volume is less than 1.5 mL) and seal with parafilm.CRITICAL: MOX-HCl solution should be prepared fresh daily for optimal results, though it be stored up to a week in a desiccator at room temperature (20°C–22°C). Discard any leftover solution.CRITICAL: Clean and maintain the Hamilton syringe before and after each use by aspirating and discarding the needle wash three times. This ensures optimal performance and longevity by preventing sample residue from sticking.Note: Avoid wastage by preparing only the necessary volume of MOX-HCl. For example, 10 samples require 50 μL MOX-HCl each (see Part 2, point 9 below), thus 10 × 50 = 500 μL MOX-HCl. However, it is advisable to prepare slightly more than the exact volume needed (an additional 100 μL is recommended). Prepare 600 μL by dissolving 12 mg MOX-HCl in 600 μL pyridine. Avoid preparing less than 500 μL as handling very small volumes can be challenging.Note: This is a light-sensitive reaction. Switch off the fume hood light but keep the extractor fan on as per safety guidelines. Keep the solution away from light until ready to use. Use amber GC vials to further protect from light, though this is not strictly necessary due to the rapid nature of the protocol.Note: Discard expired MOX-HCl powder as it should be used within one year of purchase.13.Prepare N,O-bis(trimethylsilyl)trifluoroacetamide (BSTFA) with 1% trimethylsilyl chloride (TMCS): This reagent is purchased “ready to use” in ampoules.a.Break the ampoule carefully and transfer the reagent into a GC vial using a clean Hamilton syringe.b.Cap the vial tightly and seal with parafilm to prevent evaporation.Note: When retrieving the solution, pierce the cap’s septum with a clean syringe instead of removing or puncturing the parafilm, to maintain sterility and prevent exposure to atmospheric moisture.CRITICAL: Derivatization reagents (such as BSTFA/TMCS) are highly hygroscopic. Store in a refrigerator or a cool, dry place in a sealed container. Before use, let it equilibrate to room temperature (20°C–22°C) to prevent condensation. Never expose to air for prolonged periods, as it will compromise its effectiveness in derivatization.

steps.title: Obtain and store urine samples
steps.instruction: Collect human or animal urine ethically, record creatinine for each sample, aliquot, and store: short‑term at 4 °C (≤12 h) or –20 °C, long‑term at –70 °C/–80 °C; avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Prepare laboratory and instrument
steps.instruction: Clean work area, prepare solutions, and set equipment for GC‑MS analysis.

substeps.instruction: Wipe benchtops, basins, and fume hood with 70 % ethanol (prepare 1 L by mixing 700 mL 100 % ethanol or 736.8 mL 95 % ethanol with distilled water).
Prepare needle‑wash solution: mix isopropanol and acetone 1:1 in a 250 mL Schott bottle; store indefinitely in the fume hood.
Set Techne Dri‑block heater to 37 °C (for nitrogen drying). If separate blocks are available, set a second block to 50 °C (methoximation) and a third to 60 °C (silylation).
Place uncapped samples in the fume hood when heating.
Aliquot acetonitrile (ACN) into a sealed container, store at –20 °C for ≥20 min (e.g., 3.3 mL for 10 samples, 300 µL each). Remove 5 min before use.
Wash all glassware with phosphate‑free soap, rinse with tap water, then five times with Milli‑Q water; dry in a 90 °C oven for 1 h.
Autoclave non‑filtered pipette tips: 121 °C, 1 bar, 20 min dry cycle; cool inside autoclave or dry at ≤60 °C for 30–60 min.
Clean nitrogen dryer/nozzles: soak in a fresh needle‑wash solution (not the main one) for 8–12 h, rinse with Milli‑Q water, wipe dry, and ensure complete dryness before reassembly.

steps.title: Prepare stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make internal standard, methoxyamine‑HCl, and BSTFA/TMCS solutions as described.

substeps.instruction: Internal standard 500 ppm: weigh 25 mg 3‑phenylbutyric acid, transfer to 50 mL volumetric flask, rinse boat with ~2 mL Milli‑Q water, add water to just below 50 mL, swirl, then fill to mark; sonicate 20 min if needed.
Working internal standard 50 ppm: pipette 5 mL of 500 ppm into a new 50 mL flask, fill to 50 mL with Milli‑Q water, label; store at –80 °C ≤6 months or –20 °C ≤1 month.

MOX‑HCl (20 mg/mL): weigh 20 mg MOX‑HCl, dissolve in 1 mL pyridine using a Hamilton syringe in a fume hood; transfer to a GC vial (≤1.5 mL) and seal with parafilm. Prepare fresh daily; can be stored ≤1 week at 20‑22 °C in a desiccator. For 10 samples, prepare 600 µL (12 mg in 600 µL pyridine) to have a slight excess.
BSTFA/TMCS: break ampoule, transfer reagent to a GC vial with a clean Hamilton syringe, cap tightly, seal with parafilm; keep refrigerated, equilibrate to 20‑22 °C before use.

steps.title: Aliquot urine and add internal standard
steps.instruction: In sterile LoBind 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes, process each urine sample.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 100 µL urine, vortex briefly to mix, and label the tube.
Add 100 µL of the 50 ppm internal standard solution using a clean Hamilton syringe.

steps.title: Optional urease treatment
steps.instruction: If urea removal is required, add urease and sonicate.

substeps.instruction: Prepare urease solution: dissolve 1 mg urease in 1 mL Milli‑Q water (adjust volume for number of samples).
Add 100 µL urease (1 mg/mL) to the urine tube.
Sonicate at room temperature (20‑22 °C) for 30 min with high (005) power; do not heat above 45 °C.
Store urease solution at 4 °C, stable ≤28 days; avoid freezing.

steps.title: Precipitate proteins with acetonitrile
steps.instruction: Add cold organic solvent, mix, and centrifuge.

substeps.instruction: Add 300 µL ice‑cold ACN (three times the urine volume) to each tube.
Vortex briefly for 10 s (no excessive foaming).
Centrifuge at 15 000 × g for 10 min at room temperature (20‑22 °C); place tubes with hinges outward.

steps.title: Collect supernatant and nitrogen‑dry
steps.instruction: Transfer clear supernatant and evaporate solvent.

substeps.instruction: Using a glass Pasteur pipette with rubber bulb, draw the supernatant (avoid disturbing pellet) and dispense into a clearly labeled GC vial; discard pellet.

Dry the vial under a gentle stream of nitrogen at 37 °C until completely dry (≤60 min). Position the nitrogen nozzle just above the liquid surface, adjust flow so the surface barely moves, and never let the nozzle touch the sample.
After drying, cap the vial and let it cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Methoximation derivatization
steps.instruction: Derivatize dried extracts with MOX‑HCl.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL MOX‑HCl (20 mg/mL) to each dried vial.
Cap and seal with parafilm.
Incubate in the Techne Dri‑block heater set at 50 °C for 90 min.
Remove vials, allow to cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Second nitrogen drying
steps.instruction: Evaporate pyridine after methoximation.

substeps.instruction: Dry the vials again under nitrogen at 37 °C for ~20 min until completely dry.

steps.title: Silylation derivatization
steps.instruction: Add BSTFA/TMCS and incubate.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL BSTFA with 1 % TMCS to each vial.
Cap and seal with parafilm.
Incubate at 60 °C for 60 min in the heater.
Cool to room temperature; if the sample appears jelly‑like, consult troubleshooting.

steps.title: Transfer to GC vials with insert
steps.instruction: Move derivatized extracts into final GC vials.

substeps.instruction: Using a glass Pasteur pipette, transfer the derivatized liquid into a clean glass vial insert.
Place the insert back into the original GC vial and cap.

steps.title: Prepare autosampler run order
steps.instruction: Organize vials for GC analysis.

substeps.instruction: Compile a run‑order list including sample names, system blanks (SB), extraction blanks (EB), quality controls (QC), and fatty acyl methyl ester (FAME) standards (beginning and end of each batch).
Load vials onto the autosampler tray in the exact order; verify that no condensation is present on caps (wipe with paper towel if needed).
If condensation forms on the tray, tip the tray over a basin to discard water and wipe dry.

steps.title: Set up GC×GC‑TOFMS instrument
steps.instruction: Configure the LECO Pegasus 4D (or equivalent) with the parameters below.

substeps.instruction: Install primary column Restek Rxi‑5Sil (28.2 m × 250 µm ID, 0.25 µm film) and secondary column Restek Rxi‑17 (1.3 m × 250 µm ID, 0.25 µm film).
Carrier gas: purified He at 1.4 mL/min (constant flow).
Inlet septum purge flow: 3 mL/min; inlet temperature: 250 °C; split ratio 1:10; injection volume 1 µL.
Mass defect tracking: exclude masses 149, 207, 281.
Gas saver flow: on, 15 mL/min, front inlet gas‑save timer 1 min.
Primary oven program: 70 °C (1 min), ramp 5 °C/min to 100 °C, 10 °C/min to 160 °C, 13 °C/min to 230 °C, 20 °C/min to 300 °C, hold 2 min.
Secondary oven: offset +5 °C relative to primary.
Modulator: period 3 s, hot pulse 0.7 s, cool time 0.8 s, purge pulse 0 s, temperature offset +15 °C; chiller at –80 °C.
Transfer line temperature: 225 °C.
MS ion source temperature: 200 °C (wait until set), source equilibration time 0 s.
Mass range 50–800 m/z, acquisition rate 20 spectra/s, filament bias –70 eV, detector offset +50 V, solvent delay 480 s, total run time 24 min.

Data processing (ChromaTOF): baseline tracking offset 1, smoothing 3 points, expected peak width primary 3 s, secondary 0.1 s, match required 800, S/N ≥100, integration traditional, max unknown peaks 100 000, segmented processing S/N 300, include all masses, apexing masses 2, library search mode forward 10, similarity threshold 800, MW range 50–800, mass threshold 10.

steps.title: Inject samples and acquire data
steps.instruction: Run the prepared vials on the GC×GC‑TOFMS according to the set parameters, ensuring QC, EB, SB, and FAME standards are interspersed as planned.

steps.title: Convert raw CSV to XLSX
steps.instruction: Open the exported .csv file in Excel (it opens by default) and save it as an .xlsx workbook via File → Save As → Excel Workbook.

steps.title: Apply blank corrections
steps.instruction: In the .xlsx file, subtract system blank and extraction blank peak areas from each sample to remove non‑biological signals.

steps.title: Normalize to internal standard
steps.instruction: For each compound, divide its peak area by the peak area of the 50 ppm 3‑phenylbutyric acid internal standard in the same sample, then multiply by the IS concentration factor (3.04 µmol L⁻¹, derived from 50 ng µL⁻¹ ÷ 164.2 g mol⁻¹).

steps.title: Normalize to creatinine
steps.instruction: Divide each IS‑normalized concentration (µmol L⁻¹) by the sample’s creatinine value (mmol L⁻¹) to express results as µmol mmol⁻¹ creatinine (or µmol µmol⁻¹ creatinine).

steps.title: Apply 50 % zero filter
steps.instruction: In Excel, remove any compound that shows zero intensity in >50 % of the samples within a group.

steps.title: Assess and correct batch effects
steps.instruction: Export the cleaned .xlsx as .csv, load into MetaboAnalyst, perform PCA on QC samples to visualise batch clustering; if needed, apply MetaboAnalyst batch correction or manual quantile normalization in Excel.

steps.title: Apply 50 % QC‑CV filter
steps.instruction: Calculate coefficient of variation for each compound across QC replicates; remove compounds with CV > 50 %.

steps.title: Export final dataset
steps.instruction: Save the fully processed data as a .csv file for downstream statistical analysis in MetaboAnalyst or other platforms.
